visible_symptoms: faint yellow vein clearing along the midrib and lateral veins
slight upward waviness at the leaf tip margin
leaf blade otherwise predominantly green
small reddish mark at the petiole junction
captions: Faint yellow tracing follows the veins; the tissue between them keeps a steady green.
Just the tip edge curls upward slightly; the rest of the lobe lies flat.
Vein clearing is limited to the midrib and the branches running off it — the lobe margins haven't picked up any discoloration yet.
Someone's fingers hold the stem steady against a blurred backdrop of soil and grass, and the leaf itself gives little away until you focus on the pale lines running along its veins.
Take away the vein yellowing and there'd be nothing else here to flag.

visible_symptoms: both side lobes curl/cup upward, leaving the leaf non-flat
fine dark stippling across the leaf surface
faint pale tracing along the main veins
captions: Both side lobes have curled inward at the same time, leaving the whole leaf cupped rather than flat.
A light dusting of dark speckles covers the blade.
The curling isn't confined to one edge — it pulls at the margins on both sides of the leaf evenly.
Pinched between two fingers, the leaf doesn't sit flat the way a healthy one would; the surface dips and rises slightly, and faint yellow lines trace the main veins underneath the speckling.
Compared to a flat, unaffected leaf, this one has a noticeably puckered, bowl-like surface.

visible_symptoms: extensive magenta/crimson patches between major veins
yellow chlorotic halo ringing the red patches
dark brownish-purple necrotic speckling inside several red patches
veins remain green while surrounding tissue is discolored
leaf margin tinged red-brown
captions: Deep magenta patches spread across nearly every section between the veins, each one rimmed with a band of yellow.
Several of the red zones have gone dark and gritty at the center, almost necrotic-looking.
The reddening follows the spaces between the major veins fairly faithfully; the veins themselves stay a clean green even as everything around them shifts through yellow into deep pink and red.
Very little uniform green is left on this leaf — it's now a patchwork of red, yellow, and the darker, almost burnt-looking centers within some of the larger patches.
Barely any of the original green remains untouched along the outer half of the leaf.

visible_symptoms: irregular pale cream/white blotches across multiple lobes
one lobe almost entirely white
blotch borders cut across veins rather than following them
reddish petiole base visible
captions: One whole lobe has faded to near-white.
The pigment loss doesn't respect the veins at all — pale patches cut straight across them in places.

Out of the three visible lobes, the one on the right has lost almost all its green, the middle lobe is mostly pale with only thin green lines tracing the veins, and the left lobe still holds onto a mix of green and cream blotching.
Still attached to the plant, with the dark soil and grass around it making the bleached sections of the leaf stand out even more.
Next to the green leaves nearby, this one looks almost ghostly in patches.

visible_symptoms: one lobe nearly all white/cream
middle lobe partly pale
third lobe more mottled with green dominant
irregular cream patches not bound by veins
captions: The right-hand lobe has gone almost entirely cream-colored, with barely a trace of green left in it.
The narrow lobe pointing toward the soil is the palest of the three.
Pale blotching runs unevenly across all three lobes, heaviest on the right side and tapering off toward the left, where green still dominates.
From above, the leaf reads as a mix of healthy green and bleached-out sections, with no clear boundary between the two.
A small bud sits in the soil furrow just below the leaf, untouched by the discoloration.

visible_symptoms: two small grayish-brown necrotic blotches near the upper-right area
irregular lesion edges
remainder of the leaflet uniformly green
captions: Two grayish-brown spots sit close together near the top right.
Their edges are irregular rather than round, blending slightly into the surrounding green.
Both lesions are clustered in the same corner of the leaflet — nothing elsewhere on the leaf looks affected.
Apart from those two blotches, the rest of the leaflet holds a uniform color with no curling or wilting anywhere else on the surface.
A small, early-stage lesion pair on an otherwise clean leaf.

visible_symptoms: one central grayish-brown lesion mid-leaf
tiny additional dark speck lower-right
slightly rugose leaf surface with prominent veins
remainder of leaflet green
captions: A single grayish patch sits just above the midrib, darker at its core and fading toward the edges.
The surface looks faintly wrinkled around the main veins.
Just one lesion, plus a tiny dark speck further down.
The deep green color and slightly textured surface carry through nearly the whole leaflet, broken only by the single lesion near the center.
Laid flat on a plain gray surface for the photo, the one lesion is easy to spot in an otherwise even green leaflet.

visible_symptoms: larger tan-brown lesion at the lower tip reaching the leaf margin
darker brown/black specks embedded within the lesion
couple of tiny additional dark dots elsewhere
remainder of leaflet glossy green
captions: A tan-brown lesion has taken over the lower tip.
The damaged area reaches all the way to the leaf margin, where the tissue looks dried out.
Scattered tiny dark dots show up elsewhere on the leaf, but the main lesion is concentrated at one end.
Out of the three potato leaflets here, this one carries the most visible damage — the lesion at the bottom is larger and darker at its center, with flecks of black embedded in the brown.
Noticeably more advanced than a leaf with just a couple of small spots.

visible_symptoms: yellow chlorotic mottling across the left/lower-left half of the leaflet
slightly fuzzy texture within the affected zone
right half remains green
serrated leaf margin intact
captions: The left half of the leaflet has turned a dull yellow; the right half still holds its green.
The serrated edges are still intact, just discolored on one side.
Yellowing spreads unevenly from the base toward the tip, heaviest along the lower-left portion and thinning out as it crosses toward the green half.
There's a slightly fuzzy, uneven texture to the yellowed section that the green half doesn't have.
Set against a plain gray backdrop, the color split down the middle is hard to miss.

visible_symptoms: subtle yellow speckling near the center-right close to the midrib
remainder of leaflet mostly green
short petiole visible
captions: Faint yellow speckling sits just right of the midrib.
The leaflet's outline and pointed tip are unaffected — the change is purely in color.
Limited to a small patch near the center.
Held by its short stem, this leaflet reads as plain green from a distance, and it takes a closer look to notice the light mottling near the main vein.
A much milder case than the more heavily yellowed leaflets nearby.

visible_symptoms: faint pale/tan blotching near the mid-left margin
remainder of leaflet dark green and glossy
captions: A pale tan smudge sits along the left margin.
The lobed, elongated shape of the leaflet is otherwise clean and undistorted.
Just the one small discolored patch near the edge.
Dark green and glossy across nearly its whole surface, this leaflet keeps its trouble confined to a small faded patch along one margin.
A tiny dark speck on the background is just debris, not part of the leaf.

visible_symptoms: sharp yellow chlorotic patch covering the upper-right lobe
lower-left lobes remain green
slightly textured/fuzzy yellowed area
small petiole and stem visible
captions: The upper-right lobe has turned a clear yellow, a sharp contrast next to the green lobes below it.
Each lobe of this small leaflet cluster is affected differently.
Color change is confined to one lobe; the two lower ones stay green, giving the whole cluster a lopsided look.
There's a slightly rough, textured feel to the yellowed lobe that the green ones don't share.
The contrast between the yellow and green lobes is sharper here than in the other tomato samples.

visible_symptoms: small tan-brown raised spots along the upper-right margin and near the midrib
lower half of the leaf clean
remainder dark glossy green
captions: Small tan-brown dots dot the upper edge of the leaf.
Each spot sits slightly raised rather than flat on the leaf surface.
The spotting clusters along the upper-right margin, with one or two stray marks closer to the midrib; the lower half stays completely clean.
The leaf keeps its deep, glossy green color everywhere except for that scattering of small lesions.
Far less affected than the more heavily spotted pepper leaves in this set.

visible_symptoms: overall yellow-green chlorosis across the whole leaf
scattered small dark brown/black speckled spots lower-center
one larger tan blotch near the center
small notch missing from the margin (likely incidental, not disease-related)
captions: The whole leaf has shifted from green to a pale yellow-green.
A notch is missing from the right margin, likely from something other than the disease itself.
Dark speckled spots are scattered loosely across the lower-center area, with one larger tan blotch standing out among the smaller dots.
Unlike the darker green pepper leaves elsewhere in this batch, this one has faded considerably on top of picking up the dark spotting.
Among the bell pepper samples here, this looks like the most advanced case.

visible_symptoms: overall yellow-green leaf color
darker brown/black necrotic patches along the upper-left and lower-left margins
scattered tiny dark specks across the surface
margin slightly curled and dried near the necrotic patches
captions: Yellow-green has replaced the normal dark green across nearly the whole leaf.
The margin looks slightly dried and curled near the darker patches.
Necrotic brown-black patches sit at both the top-left and bottom-left edges; small dark specks are sprinkled more lightly across the rest of the surface.
Between the overall yellowing and the darker margin damage, very little of the original green is left.
Similarly advanced to the other heavily yellowed pepper leaf in this set, though the necrotic patches sit at different spots on the margin.

visible_symptoms: mostly healthy dark green glossy leaf
small brown lesions concentrated near the upper-left margin
one tiny dark mark near the lower-right edge
captions: A few small brown marks sit near the upper-left edge.
The leaf's rounded shape and glossy surface are otherwise undisturbed.
Just a handful of spots, concentrated near one margin.
Compared to the other pepper leaves here, this one has held onto its deep green color almost entirely, with only minor lesion activity near one edge.
By far the cleanest-looking bell pepper leaf in this group.
